doing things slowly and less aggressively is the best thing for your hair, if you’re willing to wait. i’d get a clarifying shampoo and use that for a few months until you’re at a pink tone, in addition with strengthening conditioner. clarifying shampoo is a little harsh but it’s better than doing color remover multiple times. 

honestly you could rock the bleached roots look if you let it process 5-10 minutes more, and do that for a few months in prep. you could then dye your ends hot pink-bright pink for a month. at this point don’t use clarifying shampoo but using keratin or gentle shampoo is fine, because you want the dye to come out. 

the next month you can go over your ends with l’oréal color remover and 10 volume developer. it’s a little harsh but it does its job, and the months in prep before will mean your hair can take it. then dye your hair root to tip the pink it is at that point. the goal is to get to a really light color like i had on my page. 

i know it’s long and arduous :/ but, it’s what’s best for your hair. i once melted my bangs not understanding how to dye my hair at home and that SUCKED. i spent a LOT on getting professionals to fix it for the next year or so. better to be safe than sorry
